newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher as Gulf fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher as Gulf fears ease.

text.p: Taiwan share prices began to rebound from a nervous recent downturn to finish higher on Thursday as investors shrugged off worries over the Iraq military conflict, brokers said.
The weighted index ended up 76.18 points or 1.22 percent at 6,304.96. Turnover was a moderate T$39.05 billion.
"Bargain-hunting emerged as investors feel the market seems to have over-reacted to the tensions in Iraq," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
Michael Hung of Nikko Securities was similarly bullish: "We are almost certain there will not be a second Gulf war."
Brokers said the market had expected and already discounted a typhoon-related annual jump of 5.05 percent in August consumer prices, which was reported late in the session.

Recent gainers, electronics, continued to draw buying interest from institutional investors, with the most actively traded issue, Acer Inc, up 20 cents or 0.5 percent to T$39.9. Macronix gained T$1.2 or 3.47 percent to T$35.8.
Brokers said the new Securities and Exchange Commission chief, Lu Tung-ying, who took up the watchdog post on Thursday, was expected to crack down on market speculation.
"The market likes to call him Captain Lu. He will be very tough on stock speculation, but I don't think that will have a significant impact on the overall market," Nikko's Hung said.
Financial stocks were strong, with China Bills rising T$1 or 4 percent to T$26.
Brokers saw room for the index to rise on Friday, but said it would be difficult to test 6,400 points unless turnover rises sharply.
A range of 6,250-6,400 was seen for Friday.
